title: Europol-coordinated operation disrupts 57 illegal IPTV services and traces crypto payments
date_note: BleepingComputer says Europol announced the results in a Tuesday press release; neither page gives the operation's own dates, so the announcement day is used.
geo_basis: Help Net Security places the operation in Seville, Spain; Europol coordinated it.
summary: Law enforcement authorities, coordinated by Europol, disrupted 57 illegal IPTV services and identified websites offering copyrighted content, BleepingComputer reports. Help Net Security says the sites draw more than 7.3 million visits a year. Investigators traced over EUR 26 million in cryptocurrency transactions, with further analysis ongoing; Help Net Security says no arrests had been announced.
plain: Police coordinated by Europol disrupted 57 illegal TV streaming services and followed the crypto payments behind them, according to BleepingComputer and Help Net Security.
exec: Piracy services paid for in crypto are being traced; BleepingComputer and Help Net Security report 57 services disrupted.

evidence.quote: Police disrupt 57 illegal streaming services with 7.3 million visits
more than 7.3 million visits a year

validation.note: BleepingComputer and Help Net Security each state the core fact; Europol's own release could not be loaded (newsroom page did not render).

review.note: wording: summary said crypto payments; BleepingComputer says cryptocurrency transactions. Other facts checked against both pages
